entries.definition: In ACT, acceptance means making room for thoughts, feelings, or sensations while choosing how to act. It does not mean approving harm, abandoning boundaries, or giving up on change.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: Allowing present inner experience without making its removal a condition for action.

entries.definition: ACT develops ways to notice thoughts and feelings, make room for them when useful, and act in personally meaningful directions. Its aim is greater flexibility, rather than eliminating every uncomfortable thought or feeling.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: An approach that supports flexible, values-guided action alongside difficult inner experiences.

entries.definition: Automatic thoughts are quick interpretations of a situation. Noticing one allows you to examine its accuracy and usefulness instead of treating it as an established fact.

references.title: Beck Institute: Cognitive Model

entries.short_definition: A thought or mental image that arises without deliberate effort.

entries.definition: Behavioural activation works with the cycle of low mood and reduced activity. Choose achievable actions connected to care, connection, enjoyment, or accomplishment, and notice what happens rather than waiting for motivation to arrive first.

references.author: Dennis Greenberger and Christine A. Padesky
references.title: Mind Over Mood, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: Planning manageable activities that support engagement with daily life.

entries.definition: A behavioural experiment compares what you expect with what actually happens. The result provides evidence to reconsider a belief.

references.title: Beck Institute: Cognitive Model

entries.short_definition: A planned activity used to test a prediction.

entries.definition: Cognitive Behavioural Therapy combines cognitive and behavioural approaches. It helps people examine interpretations and try different actions, rather than assuming that a distressing thought must be true.

references.title: APA Dictionary of Psychology: cognitive behavior therapy

entries.short_definition: A therapy that works with patterns in thinking and behaviour.

entries.definition: Defusion changes your relationship to thinking. You can notice a prediction or self-judgment and choose your response without having to prove the thought false or force it to stop.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: Noticing a thought as a thought rather than automatically obeying it.

entries.definition: The cognitive model connects a situation with its personal meaning and the responses that follow. Beliefs shape those interpretations; examining them can reveal other ways of understanding the situation.

references.title: Beck Institute: Cognitive Model

entries.short_definition: An account of how interpretations influence feelings, body responses, and actions.

entries.definition: Committed action turns a valued direction into behaviour. It includes adjusting plans after obstacles and beginning again, rather than demanding perfect persistence with a plan that no longer fits.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: Taking and reviewing practical steps guided by your values.

entries.definition: Core beliefs influence how you interpret experiences. In CBT, identifying and examining an unhelpful belief can support more balanced conclusions.

references.title: Beck Institute: Cognitive Model

entries.short_definition: A broad belief about yourself, other people, or the world.

entries.definition: Dialectical Behaviour Therapy brings together behavioural approaches and mindfulness. DBT skills training teaches practical ways to manage distress, emotions, attention, and relationships; a skills website is only one educational resource, not a complete DBT treatment programme.

references.title: APA Dictionary of Psychology: dialectical behavior therapy

entries.short_definition: A therapy that combines behavioural change methods with mindfulness and acceptance.

entries.definition: Emotion Mind gives priority to emotional information. Other facts or longer-term goals can become harder to consider.

references.author: Marsha M. Linehan
references.section: Mindfulness Handout 3: Wise Mind - States of Mind
references.title: DBT Skills Training Handouts and Worksheets, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: A state in which feelings and urges strongly guide your response.

entries.definition: HOW Skills describe how to practise a WHAT skill. These qualities can be used together.

references.author: Marsha M. Linehan
references.section: Mindfulness Handout 5: Taking Hold of Your Mind - How Skills
references.title: DBT Skills Training Handouts and Worksheets, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: The qualities Non-Judgmentally, One-Mindfully, and Effectively.

entries.definition: Mindfulness means deliberately noticing current experience without immediately judging or pushing it away. It can be practised during everyday activities, not only meditation.

references.author: Marsha M. Linehan
references.title: DBT Skills Training Handouts and Worksheets, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: Awareness of present experience with openness and acceptance.

entries.definition: Psychological flexibility combines awareness and openness with useful action. It includes changing course when needed instead of letting rigid rules or attempts to avoid every uncomfortable feeling determine your choices.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: The ability to respond to the present situation in ways that serve your values.

entries.definition: Reasonable Mind approaches situations analytically. Used alone, it may overlook feelings, needs, or values.

references.author: Marsha M. Linehan
references.section: Mindfulness Handout 3: Wise Mind - States of Mind
references.title: DBT Skills Training Handouts and Worksheets, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: A state that prioritizes facts, logic, and practical tasks.

entries.definition: In ACT, self-as-context involves noticing experience without reducing your identity to one thought, feeling, role, or story. It does not require becoming detached or losing contact with the present situation.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: The perspective from which you notice changing thoughts, feelings, and experiences.

entries.definition: An underlying assumption connects a condition with an expected result, such as expecting rejection whenever you disagree. Treating the rule as a testable prediction can reveal where it fits and where it is too rigid.

references.author: Dennis Greenberger and Christine A. Padesky
references.title: Mind Over Mood, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: A personal rule or prediction that guides how you respond.

entries.definition: Values describe how you want to act, such as with care or curiosity. A goal can be completed; a value can guide many different actions over time.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: Chosen qualities you want to bring to your ongoing actions.

entries.definition: WHAT Skills identify what you do while practising mindfulness. Choose one action to focus on at a time.

references.author: Marsha M. Linehan
references.section: Mindfulness Handout 4: Taking Hold of Your Mind - What Skills
references.title: DBT Skills Training Handouts and Worksheets, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: The mindfulness actions Observe, Describe, and Participate.

entries.definition: Willingness concerns what you are prepared to make room for, not whether you enjoy it. It can support an achievable step toward a value without requiring anxiety or uncertainty to disappear first.

references.author: Steven C. Hayes with Spencer Smith
references.title: Get Out of Your Mind and Into Your Life

entries.short_definition: Readiness to experience discomfort when it accompanies a meaningful action.

entries.definition: Wise Mind is a DBT concept for the integrated perspective that draws on both emotional experience and reasonable thinking. It supports noticing what is true, what matters, and what an effective next step may be.

references.author: Marsha M. Linehan
references.section: Mindfulness Handout 3: Wise Mind - States of Mind
references.title: DBT Skills Training Handouts and Worksheets, Second Edition

entries.short_definition: Wise Mind is the integrated perspective that draws on both emotion and reason.
